 The Packers Need To Stop Galaxy Braining Their Offensive Line
 Photo Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images 
 By Felipe Reis - October 26, 2026 
 The Green Bay Packers have been overthinking their offensive line for years, and 2026 is no different. The latest example? Making Kevin Zeitler a healthy scratch for their Week 7 matchup against the Detroit Lions.
 #Packers RG Kevin Zeitler is a healthy scratch today. He's among the inactives in Detroit.
 Full list:
Zeitler
Zaire Franklin
Kaleb Johnson
Benjamin St-Juste
Jager Burton
Donovan Jennings
 — Ryan Wood (@ByRyanWood) October 25, 2026 
 Zeitler signed with Green Bay ahead of its Week 4 matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. He hadn’t practiced all offseason and was still recovering from surgery to repair a quadriceps hyperextension, so he naturally needed time to ramp up. Expecting him to play immediately was never realistic.
 However, we’re now approaching a month since Zeitler joined the team, and he still hasn’t played a single snap. The Packers have historically been cautious about players’ health when making signings, so it’s fair to wonder what has kept him off the field for this long.
 Especially considering what happened against Detroit.
 The Packers allowed the Cowboys to pressure Jordan Love on 45.5% of his dropbacks in Week 6. Against the Lions, the offensive line surrendered 19 pressures , with right guard Travis Glover responsible for eight.
 Given the expectations surrounding Glover entering the season, he had been a pleasant surprise through his first few games. However, his performance in Detroit was a significant step backward. With the offensive line struggling and Zeitler apparently healthy enough to be listed as a healthy scratch rather than ruled out with an injury, it’s hard to see why Green Bay didn’t give the veteran a chance.
 Their decision to scratch Zeitler also fits into a broader pattern with Green Bay’s offensive line. For years, the Packers have bet heavily on athleticism and positional versatility, often assuming a player with the physical tools to succeed at one position can move elsewhere and eventually become effective. That approach can work, but it gets harder to justify when development falls short, and the team keeps struggling at key positions.
 That’s not to say the Packers haven’t benefited from having players who can line up at multiple spots. Positional flexibility matters, and Green Bay has found players who can handle different assignments across the offensive line. The problem is when versatility becomes the default solution to every roster need.
 Need a guard? Draft a tackle and move him inside. Need a center? Draft a guard and ask him to learn a new position. Those transitions aren’t necessarily doomed to fail, but they add uncertainty and can pull players away from the positions where they’re most comfortable and experienced.
 Instead of constantly asking players to adapt, the Packers should be more deliberate about acquiring players who can address their weaknesses at the positions where they need help.
 The Packers rank last in the NFL in pass-block win rate and can’t get their run game going. Keeping Jordan Love clean is their best path to offensive success, but that starts with putting the best players on the field.
 A healthy Kevin Zeitler is undoubtedly a starting-caliber guard for the Packers, so leaving him on the sideline while the offensive line continues to struggle makes little sense.
 Felipe Reis 
 Felipe Reis covers the Green Bay Packers for Zone Coverage and CheeseheadTV. He has a Journalism degree from Estácio in Brazil and shares his Packers analysis on Twitter at @Aceti_Felipe. He lives in Niterói, Rio de Janeiro.
